subject: physics
title: Damping, Forced Oscillation and Resonance
welcome_lead: Add friction and a driver — and discover resonance peaks and bridge disasters.
meta_desc: A-Level SHM adventure on damping types, forced oscillation and resonance behaviour.
final_note: Lower damping means a sharper, taller resonance peak.

concepts.def: Energy loss reducing amplitude over time.

walkthroughs.body_html: Light: amplitude envelope decays exponentially. Heavy: slow return, no oscillation. Critical: fastest non-oscillating return — used in car suspensions.
A driver applies a periodic force at frequency f_d. The oscillator responds with a steady-state amplitude depending on f_d, natural frequency f_0 and damping.
When f_d = f_0, amplitude peaks. Less damping → sharper, taller peak. Examples: Tacoma Narrows bridge, microwave heating water at 2.45 GHz, MRI scanners.
